commit.message:
Fuse Qwen3.5 Q/K/V projections by default (#2645)

## Description

Qwen3.5/3.8 full-attention layers always exported three Q/K/V
projections. There were two reasons:
- `Qwen35TextModel` turned packing off, because its `q_proj` is twice as
wide (it also carries a per-head output gate).
- The base paged-attention path refuses packing whenever Q/K norm is
present.

This PR makes the Qwen3.5 builder emit one packed `MatMul`/`MatMulNBits`
followed by a `Split`, for both paged and GQA exports. The split widths
come from the real `q_proj` width. QKV fusion is controlled by
`fuse_qkv`, which defaults to `true`; set `fuse_qkv=false` to restore
the three projections. Builder configuration version 2 exposes the same
setting as `target_options.optimizations.fuse_qkv`.

`disable_qkv_fusion` remains supported as a deprecated inverse
compatibility alias, but it is not used by Olive recipes. If both legacy
spellings are supplied, `fuse_qkv` takes precedence; structured
`target_options.optimizations.fuse_qkv` overrides either legacy
spelling.

On Qwen3.8-27B INT4 with a DFlash 2 drafter (H200, batch 1), decode step
time improves by 1.8–2.0% with no accuracy change.

## Summary of Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/python/py/models/builders/qwen.py` | Drop the
`is_packed_matmul_supported() -> False` override. On the paged path,
`make_attention_init` re-enables packing after the base class, since
this model splits Q/K/V itself before the norms. |
| `src/python/py/models/builders/base.py` | The post-projection `Split`
uses `q_proj.out_features` instead of `q_size`, so it handles the gated
Q, and derives its shapes from `make_hidden_state_shape` so it also
works on the paged token axis. Packing is skipped when a projection
carries a checkpoint's own quantization (`quant_type` `fp8`/`nvfp4` from
ModelOpt) or `exclude_from_quantization`. Packing concatenates raw
weights and would drop those scales. The new positive `fuse_qkv` option
is authoritative while the deprecated inverse alias remains compatible.
|
| `src/python/py/models/builder_config.py` | Map
`target_options.optimizations.fuse_qkv` to the exporter option and warn
when it overrides a legacy spelling. |
| `src/python/py/models/builder.py`, `src/python/py/models/README.md`,
`docs/ModelBuilderConfiguration.md` | Document `fuse_qkv=true` as the
default, the structured JSON path, and the deprecated alias. |
| `test/python/builder/test_qkv_fusion.py` | Check packing on by default
for Qwen3.5 on paged and GQA; disabling through `fuse_qkv`;
compatibility and precedence for `disable_qkv_fusion`; other paged
models with Q/K norm unchanged; natively quantized or excluded
projections not packed; and the gated Q split feeding the `q_gate`
reshape/split. |
| `test/python/builder/test_builder_config.py`,
`test/python/builder/test_precision.py` | Check structured JSON
mapping/precedence and deprecated alias normalization. |

Behavior for other architectures is unchanged. The base paged path still
keeps Q/K/V separate under Q/K norm.

## Testing

**Focused option/configuration tests after the rename**

`python -m pytest -q test/python/builder/test_qkv_fusion.py
test/python/builder/test_builder_config.py
test/python/builder/test_precision.py`

Result: 307 passed.

**Existing builder suite validation**

`pytest test/python/builder` passes. The only exception,
`test_lfm2_moe.py::test_lfm2_qmoe_cpu_executes_partial_blocks[40-64-8]`,
also fails on `main`.

**End to end**

Package: Qwen3.8-27B, INT4 block 32, fpA_intB prepacked, INT8 KV cache,
paged attention, DFlash 2 INT4 drafter with 7 draft tokens, 1× H200,
CUDA graphs on. 8 prompts per context, 1,024 generated tokens.

- The fused weights and scales are byte-identical to the separate q/k/v
tensors concatenated along N.
- A re-export with no extra option (the new default) produces the same
`model.onnx` as the fused build measured below.

| Context | Decode step time (baseline → fused) | Change | Prompts
faster | TTFT |
|--------:|------:|------:|------:|------:|
| 0 | 20.35 → 19.88 ms | −2.0% | 8/8 | ≈ |
| 8K | 21.08 → 20.66 ms | −1.8% | 8/8 | −1.6% |
| 32K | 21.56 → 21.17 ms | −1.8% | 7/7 | −0.9% |

- Load time and GPU memory are unchanged (42.3 s vs 43.6 s load;
after-load memory −14 MiB).
- MMLU-Pro, 800 items with thinking enabled: 664 fused vs 661 baseline.
Discordant items 12 vs 9, McNemar p = 0.66.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] Default graph changes for Qwen3.5 only; `fuse_qkv=false` restores
the previous graph
- [x] Deprecated `disable_qkv_fusion` remains compatible and is not used
by Olive recipes
- [x] `target_options.optimizations.fuse_qkv` supports JSON
configuration
- [x] Documentation updated

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

+#### Qwen3.5/3.8 Q/K/V Projection Fusion
+
+Qwen3.5-family full-attention layers emit one packed Q/K/V `MatMul` or `MatMulNBits` followed by `Split`, including with paged attention, even though their Q projection is twice as wide because it carries a per-head output gate. The weights are concatenated before quantization, so the quantized values are unchanged. Projections that a checkpoint already quantized (FP8/NVFP4) stay separate. QKV fusion defaults to `true`; set `fuse_qkv=false` to keep three projections. The deprecated `disable_qkv_fusion=true` spelling remains supported for compatibility.
+
+A layer also keeps its three projections when `nodes_to_exclude` or an exact-name weight override names one of its `q_proj`, `k_proj`, or `v_proj` MatMuls, when pre-quantized projections differ in group size or GPTQ `g_idx`, or, for Qwen3.5/3.8, when the `mixed_layers` preset upgrades its `v_proj` alone.

+
+# From source:
+python builder.py -i path_to_target_model -o path_to_output_folder -p int4 -e cuda --extra_options use_paged_attention=true fuse_qkv=false

 #### Build a DSpark Block Drafter
 
 Set `dspark_path` to a DSpark checkpoint to export an auxiliary `dspark.onnx` block drafter beside a Qwen3.5 or Qwen3.8 target model. The target must use paged attention. SpecForge identifies the target layers whose outputs are tapped, while `aux_hidden_state_layers` identifies residual streams entering layers, so each configured auxiliary layer must be one greater than the corresponding `target_layer_ids` entry in the DSpark checkpoint. DSpark has no precision option of its own: its body is always BF16, and its embedding and LM head follow whatever format the target saved them in, adopted under the target's initializer names on the terms described for [DFlash 2](#build-a-dflash-2-block-drafter). `dspark_path` and `dflash2_path` are mutually exclusive, and selecting DSpark replaces rather than accompanies the target's MTP head.
